title: Business formation signals diverge from realized establishment and job capacity by sector
source_unit: US national sector, Census BFS application and BDS establishment/job flows

net_jobs_per_100_applications.unit: BDS net jobs per 100 BFS applications

observations.method: Descriptive cross-source sector comparison of 2023 BFS applications and BDS realized establishment/job flows; ratios are not conversion rates because timing and constructions differ.
observations.uncertainty: No sampling interval is reproduced; national aggregation, different source constructions, firm survival, ownership, and timing limit interpretation.
observations.counterinterpretation: High application volume does not imply durable local employment, service access, ownership, or worker bargaining power.

net_jobs_per_100_applications.unit: BDS net jobs per 100 BFS applications

observations.method: Descriptive cross-source sector comparison of 2023 BFS applications and BDS realized establishment/job flows; ratios are not conversion rates because timing and constructions differ.
observations.uncertainty: No sampling interval is reproduced; national aggregation, different source constructions, firm survival, ownership, and timing limit interpretation.
observations.subgroup: Professional, scientific, and technical services sector.
observations.counterinterpretation: Positive sector-level job intensity does not establish job quality, local access, ownership, or worker control.

observations.counterinterpretation: Positive net-job intensity does not establish worker security, service capacity, or durable firm survival.

observations.counterinterpretation: High net-job intensity does not establish job quality, local rootedness, service affordability, or worker power.

net_jobs_per_100_applications.unit: BDS net jobs per 100 BFS applications

observations.method: Descriptive cross-source sector comparison of 2023 BFS applications and BDS realized establishment/job flows; ratios are not conversion rates because timing and constructions differ.
observations.uncertainty: No sampling interval is reproduced; national aggregation, different source constructions, firm survival, ownership, and timing limit interpretation.
observations.counterinterpretation: Positive establishment entry alongside negative net jobs is a direct counterexample to treating opening activity as employment expansion.

net_jobs_per_100_applications.unit: BDS net jobs per 100 BFS applications

observations.method: Descriptive cross-source sector comparison of 2023 BFS applications and BDS realized establishment/job flows; ratios are not conversion rates because timing and constructions differ.
observations.uncertainty: No sampling interval is reproduced; national aggregation, different source constructions, firm survival, ownership, and timing limit interpretation.
observations.counterinterpretation: Applications can coexist with net job loss and establishment contraction; national sector averages hide firm and place variation.

net_jobs_per_100_applications.unit: BDS net jobs per 100 BFS applications

observations.method: Descriptive cross-source sector comparison of 2023 BFS applications and BDS realized establishment/job flows; ratios are not conversion rates because timing and constructions differ.
observations.uncertainty: No sampling interval is reproduced; national aggregation, different source constructions, firm survival, ownership, and timing limit interpretation.
observations.subgroup: Agriculture, forestry, fishing, and hunting sector.
observations.counterinterpretation: Low application volume and negative net jobs do not alone establish local service loss, cultural decline, or household effect.

boundary: This is a national sector comparison of early BFS applications with realized BDS establishment and job flows.
